key_claims.claim: Kuber's post-hoc practices: a stricter screen (P>1.5 d, 12.5-14.5 d excluded, holdout SNR>=5) 'chosen after seeing these results'; the 2/1,736 inverted count was first called an empirical FAP and corrected on 13 Oct to 'descriptive, not a calibrated false-alarm probability'; the 11 Oct extension ran in Python 3.10 with unpinned deps versus the 3.12 lock.

Chopra's audit rounds found: noise underestimated (8.2 sigma -> 7.2/7.7), missing Jacobian and correlated noise, pixel test locating brightenings as easily as dimmings, hold-out box width adjusted after a failed fold, flipped test that skipped triage, withdrawn FAP 0.01/0.2, centroid shift that was a detector-coordinate artefact, 'never searched by SPOC' false (SPOC FFI since S36/2021), UTC times off by 6.5 min; detrending window 0.75 d chosen by injection-recovery (10/16 vs 3/16, 8/16, 5/16); empirical 40-box noise cut false flags from 15-25% to 5%; 526 stars ~1.5 h on 12 cores.

eumemic's dag build: @rule(inputs, outputs, params) with ctx.input/output/param; dag.lock.json hashes inputs, params, the code of every function called and installed packages; comment-only edits don't rerun; hand-edited outputs are marked 'edited' and stop the build; undeclared reads fail; params.toml holds thresholds (fpp_max 0.5, nfpp_max 0.1, mes_min 10, ruwe_max 1.4, b_max 0.9, triceratops runs 10).
key_claims.source: https://github.com/eumemic/exoplanets README; raw pipeline/rules.py, pipeline/params.toml, tests/test_dag.py

actionable_steps: Create CLAUDE.md (<200 lines) from drafts/CLAUDE.md and .claude/rules/{provenance,vetting,publication}.md with paths: frontmatter; keep rules concrete and verifiable.

Install .claude/settings.json + .claude/hooks/guard.sh (PreToolUse on Bash|Edit|Write) from the drafts; add permission deny rules for Edit(./third_party/untrusted/**), Edit(./runs/*/prereg.yaml) and Bash(curl * -X POST *zenodo.org*); set OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 and BASH_*_TIMEOUT_MS in env.

Lay out the repo: pipeline/ (params.toml, sample/fetch/search/nulls/triage/holdout, vet/*, claims.py, manifest.py, sectors.py, tests/), runs/<run-id>/ (prereg.yaml, STATE, manifest.json, SHA256SUMS, results/, triage/, holdout/, injrec/), candidates/<id>/ evidence packs, docs/decisions/, third_party/untrusted/ read-only clones, data/ gitignored.

Write runs/<run-id>/prereg.yaml from drafts/prereg.template.yaml (Kepler Bonus cuts: join M-star catalogue to the 606,900-row source catalogue on gaia_designation; psffrac>0.5, crowdsap>0.7, >=8 PSF quarters, kic!=tpforg, exclude primaries; order by phot_g_mean_mag), commit, git tag prereg/<run-id>, deposit on Zenodo sandbox then production before the first search.

Implement pipeline.search with per-star JSON checkpoints keyed on input sha256 + pipeline version, matched inverted and phase-scramble nulls in the same invocation, holdout split written before search, and a _batch-summary + heartbeat file; choose the detrending window by injection-recovery in runs/<id>/injrec/ before freezing it.

Add .claude/skills/vet-candidate/SKILL.md (12-step ladder, tiers a-d) and .claude/agents/red-team.md (tools Read/Grep/Glob/Bash; Edit/Write/WebFetch disallowed; default refuted) from the drafts; add a reimplementer agent with Read denied on pipeline/.

Save drafts/search-batch.workflow.js as .claude/workflows/search-batch.js; run it first on a 64-star slice with args {runId, batchSize: 32, maxCandidates: 5}; expect ~2 concurrent agents on 4 CPUs (set CLAUDE_CODE_WORKFLOW_MAX_CONCURRENT_AGENTS if needed).

Run the 1,800-star Kepler Bonus pilot locally in the background (~16 CPU-h, ~4 h on 4 cores) with nohup/setsid and a Monitor watch on the log; only move to a 64-vCPU spot VM or Modal when the sample exceeds ~20k stars; adopt eumemic's --approve gate and credential-less instance pattern.

Create a Custom cloud environment whose allowlist adds archive.stsci.edu, mast.stsci.edu, exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu, exofop.ipac.caltech.edu, gea.esac.esa.int, cdsarc.cds.unistra.fr, zenodo.org (plus the default package registries); use cloud sessions for vetting/report work, not multi-hour sweeps.

Create a weekly Routine (off the hour, e.g. 09:07) running python -m pipeline.sectors --check, which uses lightkurve.search_tesscut per candidate to detect new TESS sectors, runs the fixed-ephemeris TESS vetter, and opens a PR; another routine re-runs the novelty check and reports diffs.
Implement pipeline/claims.py build/check so every numeral in report.md/REPORT.md resolves to a cited JSON field; make it a required check in the release skill and in CI.

Before any public statement: three red-team reports + written responses, independent re-derivation agreement, novelty re-run within 24 h, human-signed docs/decisions/<date>-<id>-release.md after viewing the PNGs, SHA256SUMS/manifest.json, lockfiles recorded, CITATION.cff/.zenodo.json/SOURCES.md credits (Kepler Bonus DOI 10.17909/7jbr-w430, MAST and Gaia acknowledgements), GitHub Release with bulk-data-manifest.json, human-run Zenodo publish.

Use the public-claim and professional-email templates in section 6; never use 'found a new planet'; state FPP, the open loophole, the null pass count and the catalogue snapshot UTC; link the hashed evidence pack; do not commit third parties' email addresses.

Treat RNAAS as a late step requiring a professional's prior read; note ExoFOP's 2026-08-19 policy that candidates must be published in a peer-reviewed journal and upload approval requested, so a CTOI is no longer the first public step.
